persona: Apparel art director for independent labels

designs.title: Vineyard
designs.why: From 3 m it reads right away: the arched window, the clean spaced-out VINEYARD heading and the keyline turn a busy engraving into a tidy, label-like badge that looks good on white. It has good depth, running from the grapes and posts up front, through the curving stone terraces, to the farmhouse and cypresses. The leaves, posts and house hold up crisply at full size. Two weaknesses. First, the middle terraces turn into an even grey texture of dots with no clear light-to-dark contrast. Second, the halftone is too fine to print: about 13.6k loose dots of 1-2 px (0.08-0.17 mm) and about 10k pinholes that will drop out or fill in on cotton, so the mid-tones will print muddy or patchy. The subject is also a familiar Tuscan postcard scene, so it is solid rather than distinctive for $50.
designs.fix: Rework the halftone for screen printing. Use a coarser screen, about 45-55 lpi, with the smallest dot and the smallest gap each at least 0.2 mm. While doing that, push the contrast in the middle ground: lighten the terrace tops and darken the shadows under the walls, so the curving terraces read as clear bands instead of a grey field.
